clue.text: Be quiet about group's sluggishness

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for be quiet surrounds the group

parts.note: SH is the hushing sound for be quiet
a lot is a group or batch; the 's is 'group is'

explanation.surface: A demand for silence aimed at a lazy, idle bunch of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is a noun for laziness or idleness, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: English political party make speech that's highly detailed

parts.note: LAB is short for the UK Labour Party
to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: An English party politician delivering a long, painstaking address.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate plan or design is intricate, worked out with great care and many parts.

clue.text: One youngster taking in one classical poem

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the youngster contains the second one

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
I is the Roman numeral one again

explanation.surface: A single child reading or absorbing a classic piece of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is the best-known ancient Greek poem.

clue.text: Go over, stifling unusual painter working

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the reversed go wraps around the rest
over signals turning the word go round so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of painter are put in a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to review something while suppressing an eccentric artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' sits at the end like a description of the painter, but it is the definition: a machine that is operating is working.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operating is running or functioning, in working order.

clue.text: Rugby match in the centre creates furrow

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

indicators.note: in the centre says take only the middle letter of the word match

parts.note: its central letter

explanation.surface: A rugby game played in midfield churns up a groove in the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a long groove worn in the ground, like a furrow cut by a plough.

clue.text: Maybe lying at home because trek endless

parts.note: IN means at home, as in staying in
since can mean because

indicators.note: endless says drop the first and last letters of trek

parts.note: its middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to be staying in because a long hike never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags that lying is just one way of being insincere, an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying is one form of being insincere, not genuinely meaning what one says.

clue.text: Cooks with fashionable vessel

parts.note: steams means cooks with steam
hip means trendy, fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone cooking in a stylish pot or dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' reads as a cooking pot in the kitchen scene; here it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a ship powered by steam, and a vessel is any ship or boat.

clue.text: Dad's fizzy drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal word for father
second meaning: a carbonated soft drink

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive, but it stands for 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The same short word is American slang for a father and a British name for soda.

clue.text: War game confused inapt party

indicators.note: confused says the letters of inapt are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A battle simulation that left an ill-suited party baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat sport where players shoot each other with dye pellets in mock battles.

clue.text: Boredom displayed by some teen nuisance

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sulky, troublesome teenager showing how fed up they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for listless weariness and dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Doctor with cry of approval, over-the-top, about opera

parts.note: to rig is to doctor or tamper with
ole is the Spanish shout of approval at a bullfight

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A physician cheering an extravagant opera performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning opera' but it turns OTT into TTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a hunchbacked court jester.

clue.text: Old heartless swine in New York, prying

indicators.note: in places the old swine inside the abbreviation
heartless means losing the middle, keeping only the outer letters of swine

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cruel old brute in Manhattan poking into others' business.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nosey is inquisitive, always poking into other people's affairs.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly mounted sink in residence

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going up, so the whole is read bottom to top
in puts the sink inside the residence

parts.note: to dip is to sink or drop

explanation.surface: A bug that has climbed up into a sink at home.
explanation.walkthrough: RES is a standard short form of residence, as in estate-agent listings; in a down clue 'mounted' means the letters are read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is an eight-legged creature, a typical household creepy-crawly.

clue.text: The East European twice used arena for sport

parts.note: the Orient is the East
twice says the E for European is used a second time
a ring is an arena, as in a boxing or circus ring

explanation.surface: An Eastern European using a stadium twice for athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: Orienteering is a competitive sport of navigating across country with map and compass.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeking male teacher is married

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A wedded male academic devoted to having a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure and self-indulgence as life's main aim; the gerund here acts as a noun.

clue.text: Coach starts to execute slow smooth stroke

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, a car

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: its first letter
its first letter
its first letter

explanation.surface: A swimming coach beginning to demonstrate a slow, gentle stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' looks like a swimming stroke, but it is the gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, affectionate touch of the hand, a soft stroke.

clue.text: Mock a closing musical piece

parts.note: cod is British slang meaning mock or fake, as in a cod accent

explanation.surface: Someone ridiculing a final passage of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage that rounds off a movement or composition.

clue.text: Insubstantial meal, mostly greens, half finished

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word meal, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written, less its end

indicators.note: half here means only the front three of the six letters of greens are kept

parts.note: its first half

explanation.surface: A skimpy dinner, mainly vegetables, left half eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lacking in quantity, so an insubstantial portion fits.

clue.text: Broadcast special bands somewhere in mid-Australia

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of special are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
rings are bands, such as wedding bands

explanation.surface: A radio show featuring special musical groups from the Outback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' suggests music groups after 'Broadcast', but they are rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is the town in the Northern Territory at the centre of the continent.

clue.text: Upcoming article by Rod on emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue, upcoming means rising, so the article is read upwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a pole is a rod

explanation.surface: A forthcoming piece by someone called Rod about an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like an author's name; it is a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Excellent stand-in welcomes training run

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the stand-in contains the rest

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or stand-in
PE is physical education, training
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A first-rate substitute player warmly greeting a practice jog.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means outstandingly fine, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Try on top and bottom of this suit

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

indicators.note: in a down clue, top and bottom of means the first and last letters of this

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An invitation to try on the jacket and trousers of this outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing to try on; it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Appease father whenever in outskirts of city

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in puts the word for whenever inside the outskirts
outskirts of means the outer letters of city

parts.note: its first and last letters
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: Calming down a parent whenever they reach the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to calm someone's anger, soothing or placating them.

clue.text: On the radio, closely follow story

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is a sound-alike

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Keeping close track of a serial story broadcast on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative or story, real or invented.
